source_text: Μεταμόρφωσις ἀνθρώποις μεμυθολόγηται· μεταμορφοῦνται δὲ παρ᾿ ὑμῖν καὶ οἱ θεοί.Δένδρον ἡ Ῥέα γίνεται, δράκων δὲ ὁ Ζεὺς διὰ τὴν Φερσέφατταν, αἴγειροι αἱ τοῦ Φαέθοντος ἀδελφαί, καὶ ἡ Λητὼ ζῶον εὐτελές, δι᾿ ἣν Ὀρτυγία Δῆλος ἡ νῦν κέκληται. Θεὸς εἰπέ μοι κύκνος γίνεται, καὶ τὴν ἀετοῦ μορφὴν ἀναλαμβάνει, καὶ δι᾿ οἰνοχοΐαν τοῦ Γανυμήδους τῇ παιδεραστίᾳ σεμνύνεται; Τί μοι σέβειν θεοὺς δωρολήπτας, καὶ ὀργιζομένους ἂν μὴ λάβωσιν; Ἐχέτωσαν οὗτοι τὴν εἱμαρμένην· τοὺς πλανήτας προσκυνεῖν οὐ βούλομαι. Τίς ἐστιν ὁ Βερενίκης πλόκαμος; Ποῦ δὲ οἱ ἀστέρες αὐτῆς πρὶν τὴν προειρημένην ἀποθανεῖν; Πῶς δὲ ὁ τεθνεὼς Ἀντίνοος μειράκιον ἐν τῇ σελήνῃ ὡραῖον καθίδρυται; Τίς ὁ ἀναβιβάσας αὐτόν, εἰ μή τις καὶ τοῦτον, ὡς τοὺς βασιλέας μισθοῦ δι᾿ ἐπιορκίας τις, τοὺς θεοὺς καταγελῶν, εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀνεληλυθέναι φήσας πεπίστευται, κατὰ τὸ ὅμοιον θεολογήσας τιμῆς καὶ δωρεᾶς ἠξίωται; Τί μοι τὸν θεον σεσυλήκατε; Τί δὲ αὐτοῦ τὴν ποίησιν ἀτιμάζετε; Θύεις πρόβατον, τὸ δ᾿ αὐτὸ προσκυνεῖς· ταῦρός ἐστιν ἐν οὐρανῷ, καὶ τὴν εἰκόνα σφάττεις αὐτοῦ. Ζῶον πονηρὸν ὁ ἐνγόνασι ἐκθλίβει· καὶ τὸν ἀνθρωποποιὸν Προμηθία καταφαγών ἀετὸς τετίμηται.Καλὸς ὁ κύκνος, ὅτι μοιχὸς ἦν· καλοὶ δὲ καὶ οἱ ἑτεροήμεροι Διόσκουροι, τῶν Λευκιππίδων οἱ ἁρπασταί. Κρείττων ἡ Ἑλένη, τὸν μὲν καρήξανθον Μενέλαον καταλιποῦσα, τῷ δὲ μιτρηφόρῳ καὶ πολυχρύσῳ Πάριδι κατακολουθοῦσα. Λίκαιος καὶ Σώφρων, ὁ τὴν ἐκπορνεύσασαν εἰς Ἠλύσια πεδία μετατεθεικώς. Ἀλλ᾿ οὐδὲ ἡ Τυνδαρὶς ἀπηθανάτισται· καὶ σοφῶς ὁ Εὐριπίδης ὑπὸ Ὀρέστου τῆς προειρημένης γυναικὸς τὴν ἀναίρεσιν παρεισήγαγε.
pass_a_gloss: Transformation is mythologized for humans; but also the gods are transformed among you. The Rhea becomes a tree, and Zeus becomes a serpent through Persephone, the sisters of Phaethon become poplars, and Leto becomes a lowly animal, because of which Delos is now called Ortygia. Tell me, does God become a swan, and take on the form of an eagle, and is he honored through the wine-pouring of Ganymede for pederasty? Why should I reverence gods who are bribed, and become angry if they do not receive? Let them have their fate; I do not wish to worship the planets. What is the lock of Berenice? Where are her stars before the aforementioned woman died? How does the dead Antinous, a beautiful youth, sit in the moon? Who has lifted him up, if not someone who, like the kings for a wage through perjury, mocking the gods, has said that he has gone up into heaven, and has been deemed worthy of honor and gift according to the same theology? What have you plundered from God? What, and do you dishonor his creation? You sacrifice a sheep, and you worship the same; a bull is in heaven, and you slaughter its image. A wicked animal, the eagle, tears with its talons; and the eagle that devoured the creator Prometheus is honored. The swan is beautiful because it was an adulterer; and the Dioscuri, the abductors of the Leucippides, are beautiful too. Helen is better, leaving behind the feeble Menelaus, and following the mitre-wearing and rich Paris. Lycaon and Socrates, who transferred the one who prostituted herself to the Elysian fields. But not even Tyndareus' daughter has been deified; and wisely Euripides introduced the destruction of the aforementioned woman by Orestes.

pass_b_english: Metamorphosis is mythologized for humans, but your gods undergo transformation too. Rhea becomes a tree; Zeus turns into a serpent for Persephone's sake. The sisters of Phaethon become poplars, and Leto turns into a lowly creature, because of which Ortygia is now called Delos. Does God become a swan, assume the form of an eagle, and gain honor through Ganymede's wine-pouring for pederasty? Why should I revere gods who take bribes and grow angry when they don't receive them? Let them keep their fate; I will not worship the planets. What is the lock of Berenice? Where were her stars before that woman died? How does the dead Antinous, a beautiful youth, sit enthroned in the moon? Who lifted him up, if not someone who—like kings bribed through perjury—mocked the gods, claimed he had ascended to heaven, and was deemed worthy of honor and reward by the same theology? What have you plundered from God? And why do you dishonor his creation? You sacrifice a sheep, yet worship the very same animal; a bull is in heaven, and you slaughter its image here. A wicked bird, the eagle, tears with its talons, yet the eagle that devoured the creator Prometheus is honored. The swan is called beautiful because it was an adulterer; the Dioscuri, abductors of the Leucippides, are called beautiful too. Helen is praised, though she abandoned feeble Menelaus to follow mitre-wearing, gold-rich Paris. Lycaon and Socrates, who transported a prostituted woman to the Elysian fields. But even Tyndareus' daughter has not been deified; and wisely Euripides brought about her destruction through Orestes.

review.notes: Pass A and Pass B both fail to correctly translate the relationship between Delos and Ortygia. The Greek text says 'δι᾿ ἣν Ὀρτυγία Δῆλος ἡ νῦν κέκληται' (because of which Ortygia is now called Delos). Pass A says 'Delos is now called Ortygia' and Pass B says 'Ortygia is now called Delos'. While Pass B is closer to the sense of the Greek, the reversal of the names in the translation relative to the Greek syntax (where Ortygia is the old name and Delos is the current name) is a critical error in both versions regarding the identity of the place. Furthermore, Pass A translates 'Τί μοι σεσυλήκατε?' as 'What have you plundered from God?', whereas the Greek 'σεσυλήκατε' (from συσλέπω) refers to plundering/gathering, but the context of the surrounding sentences in Pass A/B regarding 'plundering God' vs 'plundering from God' is slightly unstable; however, the primary failure is the name reversal for the island.
reasons: Pass A: 'Delos is now called Ortygia' reverses the Greek 'Ὀρτυγία Δῆλος ἡ νῦν κέκληται' (Ortygia is now called Delos). Pass B: 'Ortygia is now called Delos' is a correct rendering of the names but the prompt requires checking both against the source; Pass A is a definitive failure on identity/direction of the name change.
